front: What is M-mode's main advantage over 2-D echo?
back: Superior temporal and axial resolution (sampling > 1000/sec). Excellent for timing events and measuring rapid motion.

front: On a normal mitral M-mode, what do the E point, E-F slope, A point, and C-D line represent?
back: E point: maximum AMVL excursion during early diastolic filling. E-F slope: mid-diastolic closure. A point: reopening from atrial contraction. C-D line: closed leaflet during systole.

front: State the upper-limit normal M-mode values for IVSd, LVIDd, PWTd.
back: IVSd < 1.1 cm, LVIDd < 5.6 cm (varies with BSA/sex), PWTd < 1.1 cm.

front: How does M-mode measurement of chamber size compare to 2-D?
back: M-mode values are usually slightly larger (leading-edge to leading-edge convention captures more than the 2-D inner-edge measurement).

front: Give three causes of paradoxical septal motion on M-mode.
back: 1) RV volume overload (ASD, severe TR/PR). 2) LBBB or RV pacing. 3) Post-op state (AVR/cardiac surgery — translational motion). Septal thickening is preserved in all.

front: What is the most characteristic M-mode finding in rheumatic mitral stenosis?
back: Reduced E-F slope (loss of the normal 'M' shape of the mitral valve M-mode). Also: thickened leaflets, posterior leaflet moving in the same direction as anterior, paradoxical anterior septal motion.

front: What M-mode findings suggest acute severe aortic insufficiency?
back: Early mitral valve closure (before end-diastole) due to rapid equalization of LV and aortic diastolic pressures, wide E-point septal separation, early AV opening, and often a soft S1.

front: What M-mode findings suggest severe pulmonary hypertension on the pulmonic valve?
back: Diminutive or absent A-wave, prolonged pre-ejection period, and mid-systolic notching ('flying-W sign') due to transient reversal of the PA-to-RV outflow gradient from poor PA compliance.

front: How does the pulmonary valve M-mode differ between pulmonic stenosis and severe pulmonary hypertension?
back: PS: exaggerated prominent A-wave, NO mid-systolic notching. Severe PAH: diminutive/absent A-wave WITH mid-systolic notching.

front: M-mode findings in cardiac tamponade — most sensitive and most specific?
back: Most specific: RV diastolic collapse. Most sensitive: RA inversion > 1/3 of the cardiac cycle (or IVC plethora).

front: What M-mode finding suggests left-sided WPW pre-excitation?
back: Inward (posterior wall) motion BEFORE the interventricular septum, reflecting the accessory pathway pre-exciting the left posterolateral wall.

front: How does an LA myxoma appear on mitral M-mode?
back: Mass of echoes behind the mitral valve during diastole, echo-free space behind AMVL at diastole onset (time-lag before the mass enters the orifice), and diminished MV E-F slope.

front: What M-mode landmarks suggest constrictive pericarditis?
back: Septal 'shudder' or bounce in early diastole (equivalent to the septal bounce and pericardial knock) and flattening of the posterior wall in diastole (completion of most filling in early diastole).
